>_ Episode 13 · Oct 1, 2026 · 1h 40m

Pause AI? Should we? If so, how do we make it matter?

Play Episode 13 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube SpotifyApple Podcasts

In the wake of high-profile security breaches, frontier lab resignations, and mounting political pressure, the call to "Pause AI" has moved from fringe forums to Capitol Hill. But what does pausing AI actually look like in practice?

In this episode of Philosophy Programs and Prompts, Casey Hart(@OntologyExplained) and Carl Brown(@InternetOfBugs) break down the tangled definitions, ulterior motives, and policy proposals surrounding the AI pause movement. They explore whether agentic LLMs should be legally classified as malware, interrogate the PR machinery behind AI safety whistleblowers, and evaluate proposals ranging from Dario Amodei’s call to "pace the frontier" to the official PauseAI international treaty framework.

Most importantly, they tackle the critical distinction between abstract existential dread and immediate, tangible harms—asking whether regulatory obsession with hypothetical "superintelligence" is blinding lawmakers to the damage happening right now.
